Here are tips for enjoying a more colorful diet. For breakfast, drink
orange or pomegranate juice, add frozen blueberries to your cereal,
or whip together a peach smoothie. For lunch, include a handful
of baby carrots, crunch on peppers instead of pretzels, or choose a
vegetable or tomato soup. For a snack, keep dried apricots or pine-
apple in your desk, or sip on V8 or carrot juice. For dinner, smother
pasta with tomato sauce, order pizza with extra peppers or broccoli,
or choose a Chinese stir-fry with extra veggies.

Dairy and Calcium-Rich Foods

Dairy foods such as milk, yogurt, and cheese are not only quick and easy
sources of high-quality protein but also rich in vitamin D (if fortified) and
calcium, a mineral that is particularly important not only for growing
children and teens but also for women and men of all ages. A diet rich in
calcium and vitamin D helps maintain strong bones, reduces the risk of
osteoporosis, and protects against high blood pressure.
